strings.d1.s0.name: Jama Masjid
strings.d1.s0.tips: India's largest mosque. Climb the minaret for the view (separate ticket); cover shoulders and knees, and leave your shoes outside.
strings.d1.s1.name: Chandni Chowk
strings.d1.s1.tips: Old Delhi's main bazaar. Take a rickshaw through the narrow lanes and visit the Khari Baoli spice market.
strings.d1.s2.name: Paranthe Wali Gali
strings.d1.s2.tips: A lane of stuffed paratha fried in ghee, open since the 1870s, with 3-4 varieties to choose from.
strings.d1.s3.name: Red Fort
strings.d1.s3.tips: Shah Jahan's red fortress and a UNESCO site. Foreign visitors pay 600 INR; closed on Mondays.
strings.d1.s4.name: Karim's Jama Masjid
strings.d1.s4.tips: Mughal cooking since 1913, on the lane facing the mosque. Order the mutton burra and nihari.
strings.d1.b0.name: Al Jawahar Restaurant
strings.d1.b0.tips: Karim's rival across the road, for kebabs and korma.
strings.d1.b1.name: Gurudwara Sis Ganj Sahib
strings.d1.b1.tips: A Sikh temple on Chandni Chowk with free langar (communal meal). Keep your head covered.
strings.d2.s0.name: Humayun's Tomb
strings.d2.s0.tips: The Mughal tomb that preceded the Taj Mahal. Come for the morning light and the gardens.
strings.d2.s1.name: Nizamuddin Dargah
strings.d2.s1.tips: A Sufi shrine with qawwali music on Thursday evenings, set in narrow lanes.
strings.d2.s2.name: Lodhi Garden
strings.d2.s2.tips: A park among 15th-century tombs and the calmest spot in Delhi.
strings.d2.s3.name: Khan Market
strings.d2.s3.tips: A stylish market with kathi rolls at Khan Chacha and plenty of bookshops.
strings.d2.s4.name: India Gate
strings.d2.s4.tips: A war memorial on Rajpath. In the evening it fills with families and ice cream.
strings.d2.b0.name: Sodabottleopenerwala Khan Market
strings.d2.b0.tips: A Parsi café; try the berry pulao.
strings.d2.b1.name: National Museum Delhi
strings.d2.b1.tips: Harappan finds and Mughal miniatures, an indoor option when it is hot.
strings.d3.s0.name: Qutub Minar
strings.d3.s0.tips: A 73 m minaret from the 12th century, with a rust-free iron pillar. Mornings are cooler.
strings.d3.s1.name: Mehrauli Archaeological Park
strings.d3.s1.tips: A free park of ruins next to the Qutub complex, including Jamali Kamali.
strings.d3.s2.name: Hauz Khas Village
strings.d3.s2.tips: Lakeside madrasa ruins, boutiques and cafés.
strings.d3.s3.name: Hauz Khas Social
strings.d3.s3.tips: A café-bar with lake views, good for lunch.
strings.d3.s4.name: Lotus Temple
strings.d3.s4.tips: A Bahai house of worship shaped like a lotus. Quiet inside; closed on Mondays.
strings.d3.b0.name: Naivedyam Hauz Khas
strings.d3.b1.name: Dilli Haat INA
strings.d3.b1.tips: A crafts market with regional food stalls, an alternative to the temple.
strings.d4.s0.name: Taj Mahal
strings.d4.s0.tips: Take the 08:10 Gatimaan Express (1.5 hours) or leave by car at 05:00. Buy a sunrise ticket (1,100 plus 200 for the mausoleum); closed on Fridays. Shoe covers are provided.
strings.d4.s1.name: Agra Fort
strings.d4.s1.tips: The fort where Shah Jahan was imprisoned. You can see the Taj across the river.
strings.d4.s2.name: Pinch of Spice Agra
strings.d4.s2.tips: North Indian cooking in Agra, air-conditioned.
strings.d4.s3.name: Itmad-ud-Daulah (Baby Taj)
strings.d4.s3.tips: A small tomb that pioneered marble inlay work, without the crowds.
strings.d4.s4.name: Mehtab Bagh
strings.d4.s4.tips: A garden across the river, green in the monsoon months.
strings.d4.b0.name: Joney's Place Agra
strings.d4.b0.tips: A backpacker classic; order a lassi.
strings.d4.b1.name: Fatehpur Sikri
strings.d4.b1.tips: The abandoned Mughal capital (40 km away), an alternative to Baby Taj.
strings.d5.s0.name: Amber Fort
strings.d5.s0.tips: It is 4-5 hours from Delhi by train or car, so ideally stay a night. The hilltop mirror palace is reached by jeep rather than elephant.
strings.d5.s1.name: Hawa Mahal
strings.d5.s1.tips: The Palace of Winds facade. Take your photo from the café opposite.
strings.d5.s2.name: City Palace Jaipur
strings.d5.s2.tips: The Maharaja's palace and museum, at the heart of the Pink City.
strings.d5.s3.name: Laxmi Misthan Bhandar
strings.d5.s3.tips: A sweet shop and restaurant since 1727. Try the dal bati and ghewar.
strings.d5.s4.name: Johari Bazaar
strings.d5.s4.tips: A market for jewellery and block-printed fabric. Bargain.
strings.d5.b0.name: Jantar Mantar Jaipur
strings.d5.b0.tips: Giant stone astronomical instruments, an alternative to the palace.
strings.d5.b1.name: Rawat Misthan Bhandar
strings.d5.b1.tips: Pyaz kachori (onion-stuffed pastry), Jaipur's street food favourite.
strings.d6.s0.name: Akshardham Temple
strings.d6.s0.tips: A vast, modern Hindu temple complex. Phones and cameras are not allowed (leave them in the cloakroom); the exhibitions cost about 250 INR.
strings.d6.s1.name: Connaught Place
strings.d6.s1.tips: A circular market with white colonnades, at the centre of Delhi.
strings.d6.s2.name: Saravana Bhavan Connaught Place
strings.d6.s2.tips: South Indian thali and dosa, air-conditioned.
strings.d6.s3.name: Janpath Market
strings.d6.s3.tips: Tibetan market stalls and textiles. Bargain.
strings.d6.s4.name: Gurudwara Bangla Sahib
strings.d6.s4.tips: A golden-domed Sikh temple with a sacred pool and a langar kitchen.
strings.d6.b0.name: Kake Da Hotel Connaught
strings.d6.b1.name: Agrasen ki Baoli
strings.d6.b1.tips: A stepwell near Janpath, good for photos.
strings.d7.theme: Morning market and a gentle farewell
strings.d7.s0.name: Sunder Nursery
strings.d7.s0.tips: A restored Mughal garden beside Humayun's Tomb. Take a morning walk; on Sundays there is an organic market.
strings.d7.s1.name: Cafe Lota Pragati Maidan
strings.d7.s1.tips: Modern Indian breakfast and lunch in the garden of the crafts museum, for a farewell meal.
strings.d7.s2.name: National Crafts Museum
strings.d7.s2.tips: A crafts museum with master artisans at work, good for souvenirs.
strings.d7.s3.name: Delhi Metro Airport Express
strings.d7.s3.tips: It takes 20 minutes from New Delhi station to the airport, a quick goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Andhra Bhavan Canteen
strings.d7.b0.tips: A cheap, unlimited thali and a Delhi legend.
strings.d7.b1.name: Purana Qila
strings.d7.b1.tips: The Old Fort and its lake, an alternative to the museum.
strings.note0: The Delhi Metro is clean, cheap and air-conditioned, with a women's carriage. Uber and Ola are safe; bargain with auto-rickshaw drivers. Take the Gatimaan Express to Agra and the Shatabdi to Jaipur.
strings.note1: From June to September it is 38-45°C with monsoon rain: sightsee from 08:00 to 11:00 and after 16:00, spend midday somewhere air-conditioned, drink 3-4 litres of water a day and see the Taj at sunrise.
strings.note2: Monument entry costs foreign visitors 500-600 INR (35 for Indians); an online ASI ticket skips the queue. The Taj is closed on Fridays and the Red Fort on Mondays.
strings.note3: Choose street food that is freshly cooked and hot, and skip ice and raw salad. Stick to bottled water and bring probiotics against Delhi belly.
strings.note4: Take your shoes off at temples and mosques and cover shoulders and knees. Keep your head covered in Sikh gurdwaras, where food is free.
strings.note5: Tip 10%. Bargaining applies everywhere: start at a third of the first price.
